A hand-drawn colored-pencil illustration on a sketchbook page comes gently to life, like a living illustration. Camera completely static and locked off for the whole shot: no zoom, no push-in, no pan, no drift; the paper, the page edges and the drawing style stay exactly the same (colored pencil hatching and paper grain hold steady, no change in line style, no new details, no text).
Continuous, gentle, whole-body life the whole time, like three friends really playing music together: all three breathe visibly, their shoulders and chests rising and falling softly; the young man in the flat cap on the left strums his acoustic guitar steadily with his strumming hand while the fingers of his fretting hand shift along the neck; the young man on the right in the striped shirt keeps picking his electric guitar, his picking hand moving and his fretting fingers changing; the young woman in the middle sways to the music, tilts her head and smiles, her hands resting on the bench; all three sway slightly to the rhythm. No pose is ever fully frozen, but every movement stays small, relaxed and natural, and they stay seated in the same places on the rainbow bench. Her hair bun with its two pencils stays exactly as drawn in the first frame and only moves together with her head: the same two yellow pencils at the same angles, crossed through the bun, with only their two eraser caps showing above the bun (pink on one side, blue on the other, both pointing up) and their pointed ends hidden in her hair; no pencil ever points down and no extra pencil appears. Her headphones stay around her neck. The sunset glow shimmers softly and the drawn clouds drift a tiny bit. Silent.
